I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will stick with the cropping pattern I know best and trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. At my age, I want something steady, familiar, and not too risky on labor. Wheat and maize fit my land, the local weather, the irrigation conditions, and the way I already manage the year. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is stable and easy to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is usually better. I will keep fertilizer moderate instead of chasing the highest possible yield, because I care more about reliable output and controlling cost. I will plough before wheat to set the field up cleanly, then use rotary tillage before summer maize to save effort and time after wheat harvest. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat needs water at key stages here, while summer maize can use rainfall if the season is normal. I will spray only as much as needed to control the usual weeds, aphids, and common diseases, because I do not want extra expense or unnecessary field work.
